clue.text: Sponsors certain bonds

parts.note: certain means sure
bonds, things that bind, are ties

explanation.surface: Guarantors who back a scheme are offering assured financial bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sureties are people who stand as guarantors, vouching for another's debts or conduct.

clue.text: "A ship, an isle, a — moon" (Flecker)

parts.note: fill the gap in James Elroy Flecker's line describing a crescent-shaped moon

explanation.surface: A line of poetry by Flecker with a missing word describing the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent moon is curved like the farm reaping blade, so the poet calls it that shape.

clue.text: Smuggler is a queer bird!

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or queer
a runner is a bird, such as the runner duck or roadrunner

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a smuggler is an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner smuggled alcohol, especially during Prohibition.

clue.text: Two. Scots get led astray after start of the drinking? Rubbish!

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the opening letter

parts.note: TWA is Scots for two

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word drinking
astray says the letters of led wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Two Scotsmen are led off course once the drinking starts, which is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' scrambles 'led', and 'after' puts that behind the D that starts 'drinking'. The full stop after 'Two' is misleading: TWA is the Scots word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Admit undertaking has no force

indicators.note: has no says the force word is taken out

parts.note: an enterprise is a venture or undertaking
to prise is to force open with leverage

explanation.surface: A funeral director concedes his business lacks clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undertaking' suggests a funeral business, but it is ENTERPRISE; 'has no' removes PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, to allow them entry.

clue.text: Rook and heron are both for sorrow

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
an egret is a kind of white heron

explanation.surface: Two birds, a rook and a heron, are both omens of sorrow, as in a magpie rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Regret is a feeling of sorrow or remorse over something done or lost.

clue.text: Common right to switch votes in about-turn

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the turned word

parts.note: about is RE; turning it about gives ER

indicators.note: switch says the letters of votes change places

explanation.surface: Voters exercising their right change sides in a political U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' turns VOTES into STOVE; 'about-turn' is RE (about) turned to ER, holding STOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estover is a commoner's legal right to take wood from land for fuel or repairs.

clue.text: Viking leader would need pole for ferry

indicators.note: the answer would need the pole letter added to make the ferry, so that letter is missing

parts.note: a roll-on ferry lets vehicles drive aboard
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A Norse chief would need a pole to punt across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' suggests punting, but it is N, the north pole; add N and you get ROLL-ON, a ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollo was the Viking chieftain who founded Normandy.

clue.text: Canvas in which satyr is left out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A painting of a satyr leaves something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysails are small fore-and-aft sails, and sails are made of canvas.

clue.text: Models for short-term tenancies?

parts.note: a temp works short-term, so temp means temporary
lets are rental tenancies

explanation.surface: Fashion models taking brief rental agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Templets, or templates, are patterns used as guides to shape copies.

clue.text: Firm politician with ingenuity of mind seen in divisions

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
art can mean skill or ingenuity
mentally means relating to the mind

explanation.surface: A company man in parliament shows clever thinking that is evident across party splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged compartmentally is split into separate sections or compartments.

clue.text: Clean up articles imported from abroad

parts.note: LA is the French definite article, 'the'
UN is the French indefinite article, 'a'
DER is a German definite article, 'the'

explanation.surface: Imported goods from overseas need tidying up before sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported from abroad' tells you the articles are foreign ones: French LA and UN, then German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes, or figuratively to make dirty money look clean.

clue.text: Anna gives physiologist a sweet

parts.note: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian physiologist famous for conditioning dogs

explanation.surface: A ballerina hands a scientist a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anna gives' is a hint: the meringue pudding is named after the ballerina Anna Pavlova, so she 'gives' her name to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavlova is a meringue dessert topped with cream and fruit.

clue.text: Disturb poor Letts in a foreign setting

indicators.note: in shows the jumbled name goes inside the foreign word

parts.note: UNE is French for 'a', a foreign word that acts as the setting

indicators.note: poor suggests the name Letts is in bad shape and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Upsetting poor Mr Letts by placing him somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' scrambles 'Letts', and 'in' puts that inside UNE, French for 'a'. 'a foreign setting' sounds like a place abroad, but it is a foreign word.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to upset or throw into disorder.

clue.text: State to which vermin were reduced by farm cuts

definitions.text: State to which vermin were reduced by farm cuts

parts.words: State to which vermin were reduced by farm cuts
parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme where the farmer's wife cut off the three blind mice's back ends

explanation.surface: Rodents were brought low by agricultural cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farm cuts' suggests budget reductions; the farmer's wife in Three Blind Mice cut off the rodents' rear appendages with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice whose rear appendages were cut off would be left without them.

clue.text: Sheridan's work is endless for Bob or Jack

indicators.note: endless means the title loses its final letter

parts.note: The Rivals is a comedy by Richard Brinsley Sheridan

explanation.surface: A Sheridan play rambles on interminably for two of its characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is endless' drops the last S from RIVALS. Bob Acres and Jack Absolute are rivals for Lydia in that play.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Acres and Jack Absolute compete for the same woman, so each is a competitor of the other.

clue.text: One 'of Edward's enigmatic' mutants

parts.note: Edward Elgar wrote the Enigma set of musical pieces, each a changed form of a theme; a mutant is likewise a changed form

explanation.surface: One of Edward's mysterious mutant creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Enigma comprises fourteen variations on a theme, and in biology a variation is a mutant departure from type.

clue.text: Day of commemoration for Gaul, say

explanation.surface: A day to remember a Gallic warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Oak Apple Day, 29 May, marks the restoration of Charles II in England. 'Gaul, say' sounds like gall, and an oak apple is a gall on an oak.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak Apple Day celebrates Charles II's return; and the growth called an oak apple is an insect gall, which sounds like Gaul.

clue.text: Without a drink, terrier gets dry and warm

indicators.note: without says the drink is removed from the dog breed

parts.note: the Airedale is a breed of terrier
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A dog that has had no drink comes in and gets dry and warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes ALE off the end of AIREDALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry that has been aired has been dried and warmed, typically in a cupboard.

clue.text: Demolish article on Schlie mann's discovery

parts.note: DES is a French article, 'some' or 'the' plural
Heinrich Schliemann excavated the site of ancient Troy

explanation.surface: Writing a piece about the archaeologist's great find to tear it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to ruin or knock down completely.

clue.text: Not safe to insure church, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Leaving a church uninsured is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church, perhaps' sounds like an example of a building to insure, but 'perhaps' is the anagram signal for the two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means unprotected or exposed to danger.

clue.text: Put together firm note about everything arising

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: all means everything
about loosely sets the note beside the turned word

explanation.surface: A company compiles a memo on everything that comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' tells you to read 'everything' upwards, since this is a down clue. 'about' is loose, simply placing the note after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and arrange pages or information in order.

clue.text: A meteoric figure — Noel rising above it in Rome

indicators.note: above places the turned name over the Latin word in a down clue
rising in a down clue means the name Noel reads upwards

parts.note: id is Latin for it

explanation.surface: A star called Noel rises above it all in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NOEL into LEON, which goes above ID in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leonid is a meteor from the November shower that seems to radiate from Leo.

clue.text: Artist with loose' change for spray

indicators.note: change says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter uses spare coins to buy a spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose change' looks like coins, but 'change' rearranges RA and LOOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Lozenge made up by registered house physician

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for registered
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a physician

explanation.surface: A throat sweet prepared by a qualified hospital doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lozenge' suggests a cough sweet, but here it is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a diamond shape, which is what a lozenge is in geometry and heraldry.

clue.text: Edgar was an expert on the Eton game

indicators.note: on means the expert comes on, after the Eton game word

parts.note: the wall game is played only at Eton College
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone called Edgar was skilled at Eton's peculiar wall game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton wall game is a football-like game played against a wall at the English school. Edgar Wallace wrote thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific English thriller writer, creator of King Kong's story.

clue.text: Forgo, with a view to revision

indicators.note: revision means the letters of a view are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: Give something up in order to reconsider.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive is to give up or relinquish a right or claim.

clue.text: Before race, collision in car-port is off putting

indicators.note: before places the jumbled letters ahead of the race word
a collision smashes the letters of car-port is into a new order

parts.note: a nation is a race or people

explanation.surface: Delays at a crash in a carport before a race are unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off putting' looks like an adjective meaning unpleasant; read it as putting off. 'collision in' rearranges CARPORTIS into PROCRASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrastination is delaying or postponing things one should do.

clue.text: Immature oriental doctor goes. by rail with nothing on

indicators.note: on puts the zero after the rest

parts.note: E stands for east, oriental
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor
RY is an abbreviation for railway
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A young eastern doctor travels by train with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is something at a rudimentary stage, used adjectivally for undeveloped.

clue.text: Indeed, change of name had derogatory effect

annotationWithheld.why: Indeed, change of name had derogatory effect: the only parse is MEAN (anagram of name) in DEED, with 'Indeed' supplying both the container indicator 'In' and DEED, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Indeed, change of name had derogatory effect
